transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I’m here because things at work have gotten kind of, I don’t know, coordinated. Dispatch and compliance keep tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then there are these little comments on the radio that line up too well. People say it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.

And it’s not just me being sensitive, because I know how the routes are supposed to work—I’ve been doing transportation a while, and you start to notice patterns, like who gets sent where, who suddenly goes quiet when you come in. Anyway, that’s why I came in.

When you notice these patterns and comments, do you ever find yourself wondering if you might be misinterpreting things, or are you completely certain that people are definitely tracking and reporting on you?

I mean… I know people say maybe I’m reading into it, but it doesn’t feel like that. It’s too lined up. Like I’ll change a route and then dispatch or compliance is suddenly on it in the system, and then somebody makes some little comment on the radio that connects to it.

So no, I’m not completely wondering if I’m wrong. I think certain drivers are reporting on me. I’ve worked around routes long enough to know when something is normal checking and when it’s… coordinated.
Aside from these patterns and comments from coworkers, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people don’t seem to hear?

Voices? I mean… not like a person standing there talking to me, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes at work the radio is so scratchy, and the buses make noises, brakes and doors and all that, and people act like you’re supposed to catch every word through all that static.

So I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed hearing things that nobody else hears, exactly. It’s more that the comments line up, and then you start paying attention, because if you miss something on dispatch they’ll make it seem like it’s your fault even when the system was slow that day.

If someone you really trusted showed you clear proof that dispatch and the other drivers weren’t actually coordinating or reporting on you, how likely is it that you would change your mind about this?

I mean… if it was someone I really trusted, I’d look at what they were showing me. I’m not trying to be difficult. But it would have to explain a lot, because it’s not just one thing. It’s the route changes showing up, then compliance acting like they already know, and then the little radio comments right after.

So… I don’t know that I’d just change my mind right away. People can show you one screen or one report, but that doesn’t mean certain drivers aren’t still reporting things. Sometimes the system looks clean on paper, you know? Like at work they’ll say everything is “procedure,” but then everyone knows there’s the real way things get handled.
Outside of what’s happening at work, do you have any other strong beliefs that you feel sure are true but that other people say are strange or hard to believe?

Outside of work? I mean… not really like that. It’s mostly the dispatch and compliance thing, because that’s where it’s happening. Like, I don’t walk around thinking random people at the grocery store are involved or anything.

But at work, yeah, I feel pretty sure. The computer system shows things too fast sometimes, like when I change a route or something gets adjusted, and then compliance is already acting like they know. And then some driver will make a comment over the radio that’s not direct, but it matches what just happened. People say it’s normal oversight, but I’ve been around it enough to know when drivers are reporting back. It’s not just me being sensitive.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts, actions, or movements are being controlled or influenced by someone or something outside of you, rather than fully coming from you yourself?

Controlled like my arms or body? No, not exactly like that. I don’t feel like somebody is moving me around.

It’s more that at work, what I do on the route feels… watched, influenced, I guess. Like if I change something in the computer system, dispatch and compliance seem to know right away, and then the radio chatter starts up with these little comments. Not always direct, but enough that you can tell certain drivers are reporting back. People keep saying it’s just normal oversight, but it doesn’t feel normal when it keeps lining up like that.
Do you ever feel as if other people can somehow hear your thoughts or know exactly what you are thinking, even when you haven’t said anything out loud?

I don’t think they can hear my thoughts, like literally inside my head. It’s not like that.

But at work, it feels like they know what I’m going to do or what I just decided before I’ve even said anything. Like I’ll make a route change in the computer, or even be thinking through what makes sense for the route, and then dispatch or compliance is already acting like they’re on top of it. And then someone on the radio makes one of those little comments — not direct, but close enough that it feels like they know.

So… not thoughts exactly. More like they’re tracking it through the system and certain drivers are reporting back, and then everybody pretends it’s just normal oversight. That’s the part that bothers me.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or upbeat, needed much less sleep than usual, and were more active or driven than is typical for you?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I’ve had times where I’m busy and I’ll push through, like if the schedule is messed up or there’s a lot going on, but that’s more just needing to get things done.

Energized and not needing sleep for days… I don’t know. I’m usually tired if I don’t sleep. Sometimes I’ll stay up too late thinking about stuff, or I’ll get on my phone and then it’s suddenly late, but that’s not really the same as feeling great or super driven. 

So… no, not that I’ve noticed.
How much have these worries about dispatch and the other drivers been affecting your day-to-day life, for example your ability to work, relax, or enjoy things outside of work?

It’s… it’s been messing things up more than I want to admit. At work especially. I keep trying to double-check everything because I don’t want them twisting what I did, and then I end up falling behind on the route reports. And sometimes when I give instructions, I guess they come out confusing, because drivers complain that I’m not being clear.

And then at home, it follows me there too. Like I’ll be trying to make dinner and then I start thinking about what somebody said on the radio, or whether I missed something in the system, and suddenly I haven’t done anything. My husband’s had to take over meals and phone calls and just basic planning stuff, like appointments or what we’re doing that day.

I mean, I still go to work, mostly, but it’s not like before. I don’t really relax much. Even when we watch something, I’m half paying attention, half thinking about work.
Has there ever been a moment, even briefly, when you thought to yourself, "Maybe I’m wrong about them coordinating and reporting on me"?

I mean… maybe for like a second, if someone says, “That’s just normal oversight,” I’ll try to tell myself that. Like, okay, maybe compliance is just checking the system because that’s their job.

But then something happens again — I make a route change, or I’m thinking through one, and then there’s some little comment on the radio, or a driver acts like they already know what I did. And it’s not just one thing, it’s the pattern. That’s what people don’t get.

So I guess I’ve wondered if I’m reading too much into it, but it doesn’t last. Because it keeps lining up too neatly. Certain drivers are reporting back, and dispatch and compliance can see it through the computer, and then everyone acts like I’m supposed to believe it’s coincidence.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a well‑systematized, persistent persecutory belief that dispatch, compliance, and certain drivers are covertly tracking and reporting on her, despite reassurance from others. She shows high conviction, organizes many events into this explanatory system, and is only minimally doubtful even when confronted with alternative explanations. There are no hallucinations, thought insertion, thought broadcasting, or passivity phenomena, and no history of mood episodes or broader disorganization. The delusional content is circumscribed to work and non‑bizarre (possible in real life but untrue), with clear functional impairment at work and at home. This fits a persecutory type delusional disorder (F22) rather than schizophrenia (F20.0) or schizoaffective disorder (F25.0), as psychotic symptoms are limited to a single delusional theme without other first‑rank or negative symptoms, and there is no acute, rapidly fluctuating picture to suggest acute psychotic disorder (F23). While anxiety and worry are present, they are secondary to the fixed belief and do not meet criteria for generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1).
